headline.purpose: Major section openings and the contact proposition.

title.purpose: Projects, experience, capabilities, proof, resume entries, and panel headings.

body.purpose: Narrative context, evidence descriptions, outcomes, and explanatory copy.

shadows.name: modal-drawer
shadows.purpose: Directional separation for the assistant and Effects Lab panels above their backdrop.

shadows.name: tool-label
shadows.purpose: Small desktop-only lift for the label revealed above an AI or FX dock.

motion.purpose: Advances the field guide's teal progress line as the active evidence chapter changes.

components.css: .ds-work-row { display:grid; grid-template-columns:7rem minmax(0,1fr); gap:2rem; padding:2.4rem 0; border-top:1px solid var(--field-ink,#111816); border-bottom:1px solid var(--field-rule,#d9e0de); background:var(--field-paper,#fff); color:var(--field-ink,#111816); } .ds-work-index { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:.55rem; color:var(--field-muted,#53605d); font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace; font-size:.68rem; letter-spacing:.065em; line-height:1.5; text-transform:uppercase; } .ds-work-index span:first-child { color:var(--field-teal,#0b7169); font-size:1rem; } .ds-work-body h3 { margin:0; font-family:Archivo,Arial,sans-serif; font-size:1.55rem; line-height:1.18; letter-spacing:-.03em; } .ds-work-body>p { color:#3c4845; font-family:Archivo,Arial,sans-serif; line-height:1.65; } .ds-work-body dl { display:grid; gap:.7rem; margin:1.25rem 0; } .ds-work-body dl div { display:grid; grid-template-columns:6.5rem 1fr; gap:1rem; } .ds-work-body dt { color:var(--field-muted,#53605d); font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace; font-size:.66rem; letter-spacing:.06em; text-transform:uppercase; } .ds-work-body dd { margin:0; color:#273330; font-family:Archivo,Arial,sans-serif; font-size:.9rem; line-height:1.55; } .ds-work-body .ds-methods { color:var(--field-teal-dark,#07544f); font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace; font-size:.66rem; } .ds-work-row:focus-within { outline:3px solid #df9f2f; outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: Technical Lab Tabs

components.css: .ds-lab-tabs { display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(4,minmax(0,1fr)); border:1px solid var(--field-rule-strong,#aebbb8); background:var(--field-soft,#f5f8f7); } .ds-lab-tabs button { display:grid; min-height:4rem; gap:.2rem; align-content:center; padding:.55rem .72rem; border:0; border-right:1px solid var(--field-rule,#d9e0de); border-radius:0; background:var(--field-paper,#fff); color:#384440; font-family:Archivo,Arial,sans-serif; font-size:.71rem; text-align:left; cursor:pointer; } .ds-lab-tabs button:last-child { border-right:0; } .ds-lab-tabs small { color:var(--field-muted,#53605d); font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace; font-size:.68rem; letter-spacing:.065em; line-height:1.5; text-transform:uppercase; } .ds-lab-tabs button[aria-selected=true] { background:var(--field-teal-dark,#07544f); color:var(--field-paper,#fff); } .ds-lab-tabs button[aria-selected=true] small { color:#d7f4f0; } .ds-lab-tabs button:hover:not([aria-selected=true]) { color:var(--field-teal-dark,#07544f); } .ds-lab-tabs button:focus-visible { outline:3px solid #df9f2f; outline-offset:-4px; }

components.css: .ds-header { display:grid; min-height:4.75rem; grid-template-columns:auto minmax(0,1fr) auto; align-items:center; padding:0 1rem; border-bottom:1px solid var(--field-rule-strong,#aebbb8); background:rgba(255,255,255,.94); color:var(--field-ink,#111816); font-family:Archivo,Arial,sans-serif; backdrop-filter:blur(10px); } .ds-mark { display:inline-flex; gap:.55rem; align-items:baseline; color:inherit; font-weight:750; letter-spacing:-.03em; text-decoration:none; } .ds-mark span { color:var(--field-teal,#0b7169); font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace; font-size:.67rem; font-weight:500; letter-spacing:.08em; } .ds-header nav { display:flex; justify-content:center; gap:1.25rem; } .ds-header nav a { position:relative; padding:.7rem 0; color:#34403d; font-size:.74rem; font-weight:650; text-decoration:none; } .ds-header nav a::after { position:absolute; right:0; bottom:.4rem; left:0; height:2px; background:var(--field-teal,#0b7169); content:''; transform:scaleX(0); transform-origin:left; transition:transform 160ms ease; } .ds-header nav a:hover::after,.ds-header nav a:focus-visible::after { transform:scaleX(1); } .ds-header button { min-height:2.6rem; padding:.65rem .9rem; border:1px solid var(--field-ink,#111816); border-radius:0; background:transparent; color:var(--field-ink,#111816); font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace; font-size:.66rem; font-weight:600; letter-spacing:.06em; text-transform:uppercase; cursor:pointer; } .ds-header button:hover { background:var(--field-ink,#111816); color:var(--field-paper,#fff); } .ds-header a:focus-visible,.ds-header button:focus-visible { outline:3px solid #df9f2f; outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: Desktop Optional Tool Docks

components.css: .ds-tool-docks { display:flex; gap:.75rem; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-end; padding:2.25rem .25rem .25rem; } .ds-tool-docks button { position:relative; display:grid; width:3.25rem; min-width:3.25rem; height:3.25rem; place-items:center; padding:0; border:1px solid var(--field-ink,#111816); border-radius:0; background:var(--field-paper,#fff); box-shadow:none; color:var(--field-ink,#111816); cursor:pointer; } .ds-tool-docks button span:first-child { color:var(--field-teal-dark,#07544f); font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace; font-size:.7rem; font-weight:700; } .ds-tool-docks button span:last-child { position:absolute; right:0; bottom:calc(100% + .5rem); width:max-content; padding:.32rem .48rem; transform:translateY(.3rem); border:1px solid var(--field-rule,#d9e0de); background:var(--field-paper,#fff); box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(23,38,36,.1); opacity:0; color:var(--field-ink,#111816); font-family:Archivo,Arial,sans-serif; font-size:.64rem; pointer-events:none; transition:transform 150ms,opacity 150ms; } .ds-tool-docks button:hover span:last-child,.ds-tool-docks button:focus-visible span:last-child { transform:translateY(0); opacity:1; } .ds-tool-docks button:focus-visible { outline:3px solid #df9f2f; outline-offset:3px; } .ds-tool-docks button:active { background:var(--field-soft,#f5f8f7); }

components.name: Field Engineer Guide Stage
components.description: Supporting graphite-and-teal calibration stage with chapter readout, survey path, and restrained progress.
components.css: .ds-guide { position:relative; width:18rem; height:32rem; margin:0; overflow:hidden; border-left:1px solid var(--field-rule,#d9e0de); background:repeating-linear-gradient(0deg,transparent 0 3.75rem,rgba(217,224,222,.4) 3.75rem calc(3.75rem + 1px)); color:var(--field-ink,#111816); } .ds-guide figcaption { position:absolute; z-index:2; top:1.1rem; left:1.25rem; display:grid; max-width:15rem; gap:.45rem; } .ds-guide figcaption span { color:var(--field-muted,#53605d); font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace; font-size:.68rem; font-weight:500; letter-spacing:.065em; text-transform:uppercase; } .ds-guide figcaption strong { font-family:Archivo,Arial,sans-serif; font-size:.86rem; font-weight:620; line-height:1.45; } .ds-guide svg { display:block; width:100%; height:100%; } .ds-guide-grid { fill:none; stroke:rgba(174,187,184,.36); } .ds-guide-path { fill:none; stroke:var(--field-teal,#0b7169); stroke-width:2; } .ds-guide-person { fill:var(--field-ink,#111816); stroke:var(--field-ink,#111816); stroke-width:8; stroke-linecap:square; } .ds-guide-person circle { stroke-width:0; } .ds-guide-signal { fill:var(--field-teal,#0b7169); stroke-width:0; } .ds-guide-progress { position:absolute; right:1.25rem; bottom:1.5rem; left:1.25rem; height:2px; background:var(--field-rule,#d9e0de); } .ds-guide-progress span { display:block; width:72%; height:100%; background:var(--field-teal,#0b7169); transition:width 280ms ease; } .ds-guide:focus-within { outline:3px solid #df9f2f; outline-offset:-4px; }

narrative.overview:
The portfolio is a clean white laboratory record of an engineer making intelligent systems operational. It reads as one continuous field test under visual seed `4d83e73b`: Rahul's positioning, experience, selected systems, complete project archive, technical study, capabilities, proof, résumés, and contact path remain stationary, explicit, and easy to inspect. Near-black type and fine rules establish authority; restrained teal marks navigation, methods, state, and verification.

The graphite-and-teal field engineer is a supporting guide, not the subject. On wide screens it occupies a sticky calibration stage beside the evidence and advances gently with the reader's scroll. On constrained devices it becomes a static poster after the first-view facts, so mobile always presents Rahul's claim and actions first. Sparse amber and violet belong to focus, survey stations, reconstruction, and other technical annotations; they do not become decorative themes or unsupported experience claims.

The interface has one evidence model and no Build/Secure lenses. The assistant, Effects Lab, and Spatial World are optional depth layers: fixed AI and FX controls are desktop-only, while mobile exposes AI, FX, and Spatial World inside the header menu. Motion or heavy rendering may frame the reading path, but never owns it, gates it, or carries recruiter-critical information.
keyCharacteristics: White laboratory field with near-black editorial typography and hairline ledger rules.
Real experience, projects, outcomes, proof, and résumé links dominate every section.
A persistent desktop evidence-and-guide split that collapses to an evidence-first mobile column.
Archivo for claims and reading; IBM Plex Mono for methods, dates, counts, readouts, and state.
Square controls and ruled rows instead of floating cards, pills, or dashboard chrome.
Optional spatial and generative tools remain clearly labeled, accessible, and subordinate.

rules.name: The Evidence Owns the Page Rule
rules.body: White and graphite carry the page; color supports navigation, state, technical meaning, and focus.

rules.name: The Sparse Signal Rule
rules.body: Teal is restrained and amber or violet is rarer still. Never use any signal color as a large atmospheric wash or decorative gradient.

rules.name: The One Evidence Model Rule
rules.body: Do not reintroduce Build/Secure palettes, switches, or content lenses. Security evidence lives in the same hierarchy as every other discipline.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Archivo makes claims and carries the evidence; IBM Plex Mono measures and labels it. Never set long narrative paragraphs in mono.

rules.name: The Claim Before Metadata Rule
rules.body: Large Archivo establishes what matters before small mono explains when, how, or where it was measured.

rules.name: The Continuous Evidence Rule
rules.body: Preserve the complete reading order and visible project archive; progressive interaction may filter or navigate evidence but must not hide the factual baseline.

rules.name: The Guide Yields Rule
rules.body: The guide may own a dedicated desktop column, but it disappears before it can compress evidence below a comfortable reading width.

rules.name: The 320px Integrity Rule
rules.body: At the narrowest supported width, preserve the positioning claim, selected-work action, résumé path, optional-tool access, and every evidence record without overlap or horizontal scrolling.

rules.name: The Flat Evidence Rule
rules.body: Project, experience, capability, proof, résumé, filter, and laboratory surfaces stay flat at rest; use rules and spacing before elevation.

rules.name: The Modal Exception Rule
rules.body: Shadow is reserved for temporary layers that must separate from the reading surface, never for making ordinary content look clickable.

rules.name: The Ruled Ledger Rule
rules.body: Group evidence with shared top and bottom rules instead of rounding each record into an isolated card.

rules.name: The Geometry Must Measure Rule
rules.body: Lines, diamonds, trajectories, points, and reconstruction marks must communicate a guide position, technical layer, measurement, or state—not generic technological decoration.

rules.name: The Optional Tools Rule
rules.body: Assistant, effects, and spatial experiences may deepen the portfolio, but no recruiter-critical fact, proof, résumé, or contact action may exist only inside them.

rules.name: The Motion Never Competes Rule
rules.body: Motion may explain progress or temporary state; it must never loop around, move, blur, or delay reading content.

dos: Do lead with Rahul's positioning, explicit actions, current evidence, and real work.
Do preserve the continuous story: position → selected work → experience → all projects → technical lab → capabilities → proof → résumés → contact.
Do use white space, one-pixel rules, and typographic hierarchy to organize dense evidence.
Do keep teal restrained and reserve amber and violet for focus or technical annotation.
Do keep the field engineer in a supporting desktop guide role and use the static evidence-first fallback on constrained devices.
Do expose AI, FX, and Spatial World in the mobile header menu while keeping fixed AI and FX controls desktop-only.
Do preserve visible focus, semantic landmarks, keyboard-operable filters and tabs, truthful disclaimers, and the complete project archive.
Do make reduced motion a static, fully readable version of the same experience.
donts: Don't reintroduce Build/Secure lenses, lens-specific palettes, or lens-dependent evidence.
Don't convert the portfolio into warm notebook paper, tinted chapter themes, a camera-rail journey, or a wall of rounded cards.
Don't let the guide, generated media, optional tools, or Three.js occupy the evidence hierarchy.
Don't imply professional robotics, SLAM, localization, mapping, or Gaussian-splatting delivery from the technical motifs or synthetic study.
Don't use generic AI gradients, neon or glitch styling, game HUD chrome, stock robots, or meaningless equations.
Don't set long reading copy in IBM Plex Mono or use low-contrast microtype for essential information.
Don't let motion, pointer precision, WebGL, or optional panels gate reading, résumé access, proof, or contact.
